text: [curious] The Arabic word for coffee... used to mean [shouting] WINE!
The Arabic word for coffee used to mean [shouting] WINE!
Qahwa. Old Arabic dictionaries say it meant wine, because it puts you off your food.
Then, in the fourteen-hundreds, Sufis in Yemen drank a dark brew of coffee beans to stay awake for their night prayers. And the name moved over: qahwa.
It spread to Makkah, Cairo and Istanbul, where it became kahve. The Dutch said koffie, and by 1582, English had: coffee.
Your turn. A masjid is the place of sujood. So what's this?
A CAFE! The place of qahwa.
So every coffee you order is a little bit of Arabic. How do you take yours? Comment below!
In the 1400s, Sufis in Yemen drank coffee to stay up for night prayers... and called it: qahwa.
Istanbul made it kahve, the Dutch made it koffie, and by 1582, English had: coffee.
The Arabic word for coffee used to mean... wine.
Old Arabic dictionaries say it meant wine, because it takes away your appetite.
Then, in the fourteen-hundreds, Sufis in Yemen drank a dark brew made from coffee beans, to stay awake for their night prayers.
And they gave it the old name: qahwa.
From Yemen it travelled to Makkah and Cairo, then to Istanbul, where it became kahve.
Ships carried it to Europe. The Dutch said koffie, and by fifteen eighty-two, English had a new word: coffee.
